newsitem.title: USA: Airfares could buoy US March core CPI--Jackman.
newsitem.headline: Airfares could buoy US March core CPI--Jackman.

text.p: Labor Department economist Patrick Jackman on Tuesday said it was possible that increases in air fares because of the reimposition of the 10 percent airline tax could buoy the core rate of the March Consumer Price Index.
In a telephone interview, Jackman also said it was likely that levels of increases in food and energy in February would not be repeated in March and that this could moderate the overall CPI.
"There could be some slight uptick (in the core rate) because of reimposition of the airline fare tax," he said.
In addition, Jackman said that an early spring and summer on the East Coast could bring about some increases in apparel costs as warm weather lines are introduced earlier in retail stores.
"It is a timing issue," he said, "since seasonal factors will not have anticipated the earlier introduction."
The CPI rose 0.3 percent in February, while the core rate, which excludes food and energy and is considered a better indicator of inflationary trends, rose 0.2 percent.
Food prices in the month rose 0.3 percent, mainly because of a jump in fresh vegetable prices, which rose 8.9 percent.
He also said there there was the prospect of an easing of energy prices, which rose 0.3 percent in February, and that this could benefit the overall inflation number for March.
